parsed.explanation: The quoted "finite blocker" fact appears verbatim in the write-up and is used, with no extra hypotheses, to derive the Finite-transversal lemma. The objection's family satisfies its hypotheses: F_i = {c, a_i, b_1,...,b_{i-1}} are finite, pairwise intersecting (all contain c), and C = F_1 has size 2. Yet B_n = {a_1,...,a_n,b_n} is a transversal (it meets F_i via a_i for i<=n, and via b_n for i>n since n<=i-1) and is minimal: deleting a_j (j<=n) leaves F_j unmet (b_n not in F_j as n>j-1), and deleting b_n leaves F_{n+1} unmet. So infinitely many distinct minimal finite transversals exist, refuting the fact, and by the same example the Finite-transversal lemma's conclusion (finitely many B_j) fails. Since all finiteness in the write-up (obligation F) rests on this lemma, the gap is fatal; the text supplies no bounded-size or small-prime argument elsewhere.
